title: Multicenter characterization of enterocolitis associated with BCMA-directed CAR T cell therapy
desc: Immune effector cell-associated enterocolitis (IEC-EC) is a delayed toxicity of ciltacabtagene autoleucel. The US Multiple Myeloma Immunotherapy Consortium retrospectively adjudicated 54 suspected cases from 8 institutions: 41 were IEC-EC (31 confirmed by anti-camelid variable heavy-chain immunohistochemistry, 10 probable). Through September 2025, cumulative incidence was 3.0% (39 of 1,308 ciltacabtagene autoleucel recipients; 95% CI 2.1–4.1%); 12-month competing-risk incidence was 3.0% (95% CI 2.1–4.1%). Median symptom onset was 75 days after infusion. Grade ≥3 diarrhea occurred in 85% (34 of 40 with diarrhea); 73% (30 of 41) required parenteral nutrition. Despite normal upper endoscopy in 41% (9 of 22), duodenal biopsies showed villous blunting, apoptotic bodies and a dense cytotoxic T cell infiltrate, CD4^+ in 61% (19 of 31), CD8^+ in 26% (8 of 31) and mixed in 13% (4 of 31). A dominant T cell clone was detected in 76% (13 of 17 tested). Delayed neurotoxicity co-occurred in 41% (17 of 41). At last follow-up, 32% (13 of 41) resolved, 27% (11 of 41) had ongoing symptoms and 41% (17 of 41) died with active IEC-EC. Combined biologic and T cell-directed therapy yielded the highest resolution (55%, 6 of 11) in small subgroups. IEC-EC is potentially fatal and requires systematic evaluation and early directed therapy. In a large multicenter case series, only 32% of patients who developed immune effector cell-associated enterocolitis following treatment with BCMA-directed CAR T cells had achieved disease resolution at last follow-up, with some deaths directly attributable to complications of this disorder.

title: Metastatic Prostate Cancer Treatment Variation in Veterans.
desc: [JAMA network open] Not all men with metastatic castration-sensitive prostate cancer (mCSPC) receive the recommended combination therapy of androgen deprivation therapy (ADT) plus an androgen receptor pathway inhibitor (ARPI) and/or chemotherapy. To determine factors associated with combination therapy use among veterans with mCSPC in the national Veterans Health Administration (VHA) system. This cohort study included US veterans diagnosed with mCSPC between January 1, 2023, through December 31, 2024, who were followed up through June 30, 2025. National multicenter data were obtained from the VHA electronic health record, community care settings (private care paid with VHA benefits), and Medicare. All included veterans were identified through a validated natural language processing algorithm, were followed up in the VHA for at least 2 years prior to their metastatic diagnosis, were provided ADT within the first 6 months of diagnosis, and received no prostate cancer-directed therapy in the year prior to diagnosis. Clinical factors (eg, comorbidities, frailty, prostate cancer burden at diagnosis) and nonclinical factors (eg, annual household income, neighborhood disadvantage) were investigated to determine their association with the outcome. The primary outcome was receipt of combination therapy (ie, ADT plus ARPI [abiraterone, enzalutamide, apalutamide, darolutamide] and/or docetaxel) vs ADT alone. Multilevel logistic regression models were used and marginal predicted probabilities were reported to determine the associations of factors with receipt of combination therapy. title: Artificial Intelligence in Lung Diseases: Screening, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prognosis.
source: PubMed · Methods in molecular biology (Clifton, N.J.)
desc: [Methods in molecular biology (Clifton, N.J.)] Pulmonary diseases currently pose significant threats to global health, spanning common chronic conditions including lung cancer, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), and asthma, as well as infectious and inflammatory diseases like tuberculosis, interstitial lung disease (ILD), and COVID-19. Therefore, accurate diagnosis, effective therapeutic strategies, and reliable assessment of prognosis for pulmonary diseases are essential for improving patient outcomes and safeguarding public health. Despite the increasing availability of medical imaging and pathological data owing to improvements in detection technologies, what is becoming increasingly evident are the limitations of conventional diagnosis, which relies solely on clinicians' subjective judgment based on imaging, pulmonary function, pathology, and clinical experience. In recent years, artificial intelligence (AI) technology, especially machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL), has made significant progress in areas such as image recognition and model construction. Numerous studies have demonstrated the widespread application of AI in the screening and diagnosis of lung diseases, the optimization of treatment strategies, and prognosis assessment, revealing its remarkable ability to process and interpret complex clinical data. Although concerns persist regarding data quality, the "black box" nature of algorithms, clinical practice, and the regulatory landscape, the application of AI in lung disease research and clinical care is more and more promising. In this review, we summarize the latest advances of AI in the diagnosis and treatment of pulmonary diseases, analyze the challenges and limitations of current AI technologies ranging from data and algorithms to clinical translation, and highlight directions for future research.

title: PReMind: When Personal Memory Meets Visual Hazards
desc: Personalized vision-language assistants use visual observations and personal memories to provide advice tailored to the user. When the observed scene contains a physical hazard, personal context, such as allergies, medical conditions, or mobility constraints, can change what help is appropriate. Responding appropriately therefore requires recognizing the visible hazard and applying the relevant person's information. We introduce PReMind-Bench, a diagnostic benchmark that evaluates this combination across diverse hazards and personal-memory conditions. It separately measures memory access, grounding, abstention, and hazard response, and assesses joint success on interdependency cases. Existing models often satisfy one requirement while failing the other, and training only for safety or personalization leaves a gap in joint success. We therefore propose PReMind, a two-phase reinforcement learning framework that combines on-demand and forced-call interactions (memory always retrieved) to jointly train grounded memory use and hazard response. At 4B, PReMind raises joint success from 12.9% to 28.6% over its base on the interdependency set and improves hazard adequacy and correct abstention on the main test. Joint-success gains persist under forced-call evaluation and under a second LLM judge across three Phase II seeds; averaged over these seeds, joint success also improves on unseen hazard groups. These findings highlight the need to evaluate and train personal assistants to connect visual evidence with the relevant person's context.

title: ADSMoE: A mixture-of-experts-based transformer autoencoder for discovering multimodal Alzheimer's disease subtypes
desc: Alzheimer's disease (AD) exhibits substantial biological and clinical heterogeneity, posing critical challenges for advancing precision medicine. Existing data-driven approaches often rely on modality-specific clustering or predefined biomarker trajectories, limiting their ability to discover disease subtypes from incomplete, heterogeneous real-world data. In this study, we introduce ADSMoE, a mixture-of-experts (MoE)-based multimodal representation learning framework that jointly identifies AD subtypes as latent disease signatures while accommodating incomplete modality combinations. ADSMoE integrates a Fleximodal MoE encoder that accommodates arbitrary combinations of available modalities with a novel subtype-specific MoE decoder to capture complementary disease characteristics through expert specialization. Using data from 5,422 participants across three independent cohorts, we trained ADSMoE on the ADNI cohort and externally validated the identified subtypes in NACC and UKB without model retraining. The proposed ADSMoE identified four AD subtypes with distinct neuroimaging patterns, genetic and proteomic associations, and clinical characteristics. Benchmarking analyses demonstrated robust subtype discovery and strong biological and clinical relevance, while external validation revealed consistent subtype-associated characteristics across independent cohorts. ADSMoE advances AD subtyping by uncovering biologically and clinically meaningful AD heterogeneity from incomplete multimodal data, providing a scalable framework for disease stratification, biomarker discovery, and future precision medicine applications in AD.

title: Sparrowhawk: harnessing WebAssembly for private microbial genomics, and beyond
desc: Computational methods are a growing component of every scientific discipline, but the pace of training and expertise for using these methods has not kept up with their widening usage. Researchers expect state-of-the-art methods to be able to independently explore their results, and do so dynamically and interactively. Producing such an application which implements a new algorithm, even though it would access a much wider audience, is typically beyond the expertise and time constraints of computational method developers. Here, we show our Sparrowhawk framework can rapidly create an interactive web application to run interactive analysis on a user's machine, across a wide range of algorithms. Focusing first on genomic epidemiology, a domain with a specific need for such methods, we created novel lightweight methods for genome assembly, antimicrobial resistance gene annotation, and taxonomic identification. Our results exceed performance of previous lightweight methods, and produce results that reproduce or closely match previous analysis pipelines. By using WebAssembly, our framework benefits from not requiring installation, command line knowledge, or transferring sensitive data over an internet connection. We show how algorithms from other researchers, and spanning fields from machine learning to physics, can rapidly be ported to web tools using our framework. We demonstrate an immediate impact on microbial bioinformatics, but expect that uptake of Sparrowhawk by developers of other tools broadly will help other researchers, and create new tools for teaching and public engagement. Thanks to the broad availability and familiarity with web browser tools across society, Sparrowhawk has the potential to significantly lower the barrier to entry to advanced computational methods.

title: Bridging Brain Connectome and Clinical Notes: A Novel Multimodal Framework for MCI Study.
source: PubMed · IEEE transactions on medical imaging
desc: [IEEE transactions on medical imaging] Integrating brain imaging data with clinical reports enables the effective use of complementary multimodal information, supporting more accurate and timely diagnosis in real-world clinical settings. This approach has gained growing attention in brain disorder research, yet significant limitations remain: how to encode brain structure and function to reflect meaningful neurological patterns, and how to effectively link objective imaging data with subjective text-based reports while establishing interpretable associations. In this work, we propose a novel multimodal framework that aligns brain connectomes with clinical reports in a shared cross-modal latent space at both subject and connectome levels. Our key innovation lies in treating brain subnetworks as tokens rather than raw image patches, enabling more efficient identification of system-level associations between neuroimaging findings and clinical observations. These cross-modal associations are further fused to enhance mild cognitive impairment (MCI) prediction and provide interpretable diagnostic insights. To our knowledge, this is the first attempt to integrate both structural and functional brain connectivity with non-imaging clinical information. Experimental validation on the ADNI dataset demonstrates performance competitive with recently reported methods. Notably, despite no explicit connectome-token-level supervision, the learned connectome-text associations recover multiple relationships independently reported in the neuroimaging and clinical literature, suggesting that the framework captures clinically coherent cross-modal associations. This pioneering work advances multimodal artificial intelligence (AI) for neurodegenerative disease diagnosis by bridging the gap between neuroimaging analysis and clinical text interpretation through innovative connectome tokenization and cross-modal alignment strategies.

title: AI-Assisted Diagnosis: Big Data Analytics in Clinical Decision Support.
source: PubMed · Methods in molecular biology (Clifton, N.J.)
desc: [Methods in molecular biology (Clifton, N.J.)] With the development of artificial intelligence (AI), AI-assisted clinical diagnosis, driven by big data analytics and machine/deep learning (ML/DL), has brought great changes in clinical decision. AI enhances disease detection, classification, and treatment planning by processing diverse data such as electronic health records (EHRs), medical images, and genomics. Key applications include high-accuracy cancer screening, neurological disorder prediction, and diagnostics in ophthalmology, endocrinology, and pediatrics. Significant challenges involve data quality/standardization, model interpretability, and ethical/legal concerns. Mitigation strategies include federated learning, Explainable AI, and fairness constraints. Future directions focus on multimodal data fusion, real-time monitoring via wearables, and collaborative human-AI diagnostics. AI is positioned as a tool to augment clinicians, promising improved diagnostic precision, efficiency, and accessibility in precision medicine, contingent on overcoming technical and ethical hurdles through interdisciplinary collaboration.

title: Agreement of ASA Physical Status Classification Among Anesthesia Residents, a Large Language Model, and Senior Anesthesiologist Consensus
desc: [Newly registered clinical trial, no results yet; sponsor: Kayseri City Hospital; conditions: Anesthesia, Risk Assessment, Preoperative Care; type: OBSERVATIONAL; enrollment: 330; status: NOT_YET_RECRUITING] The ASA Physical Status Classification is widely used in preoperative risk assessment, but agreement between raters is limited, particularly between ASA II and III. This prospective observational study compares the ASA class assigned to the same patients by three types of raters: anesthesia residents working in the preoperative anesthesia clinic, a large language model (LLM), and a consensus of two senior anesthesiologists, which is the reference standard. Residents complete the standard preoperative evaluation form and assign an ASA class as part of routine care. A copy of the completed form, with patient identifiers and the resident's ASA class removed, is then given independently to the LLM and to the two senior anesthesiologists. No intervention is applied to participants and routine care is not changed. The primary aim is to measure how closely the residents and the LLM agree with the expert consensus (weighted kappa). Secondary aims are agreement among all three raters, agreement between the two senior anesthesiologists, the direction of misclassification, and how often the LLM matches the consensus when the resident does not.

title: Prospective prediction of clinical trial outcomes from public evidence
desc: Predicting clinical trial outcomes requires interpreting biological and clinical evidence in the context of a specific intervention, population and study design. Here we test whether a general-purpose large language model (LLM) can predict trial outcomes from publicly available evidence. We introduce TrialDossier, which assembles standardized evidence dossiers, and TrialOutlook, which uses these dossiers with GPT-5 to estimate the probability that a trial meets its prespecified primary endpoint. Among 694 ongoing trials with results expected within six months of cohort assembly, 69 outcomes first disclosed after forecast recording had been adjudicated by 20 October 2026. TrialOutlook achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.819 (95% confidence interval, 0.708 to 0.914) and an average precision of 0.860. TrialOutlook correctly identified 27 of 29 failures (93.1%) and incorrectly classified 17 of 40 successes as failures. We further recorded forecasts for 5,809 ongoing trials associated with US-listed companies and established a public benchmark linking archived evidence and fixed forecasts to adjudicated outcomes as they become available.

title: Localizing Unsampled Regions in Partially Sampled Pathogen Phylogenies Using Machine Learning
desc: Motivation: Pathogen phylogenies are useful for monitoring the evolution of pathogens and for detecting new variants, as it provides information that can aid public health decisions and outbreak response. Since not all infections are sequenced, certain pathogen lineages may be missing or only poorly represented in reconstructed phylogenies. Identifying these gaps could help to determine where additional data collection is required. Results: We developed a computational method to locate regions of missing samples from the observed tree alone, without sequences from those samples. A machine learning model predicts which branches lead toward the missing region. Beam search then identifies three representative paths and estimates a candidate most recent common ancestor (MRCA) of the missing region for each path. We tested this framework on 5,000 simulated phylogenies where we controlled which tips were deleted. On an independent test set, the best candidate recovered an average of 89.9% of deleted tips, increasing to 90.7% when all three candidates were combined. Predicted and true MRCAs lay on the same ancestral-descendant lineage in 91.3% of cases. We further evaluated the approach on an empirical SARS-CoV-2 phylogeny with introduced missingness. By identifying potentially underrepresented lineages, this framework could help real-time identification of missing infections and improve outbreak response.

desc: Ciltacabtagene autoleucel (cilta-cel) is a B cell maturation-antigen-targeting chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T cell product approved for relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma treatment. Previously reported cases of post-cilta-cel immune effector cell enterocolitis (IEC-EC) have been described as a severe diarrhea associated with clonal CAR T cell populations. Here we report nine cases of cilta-cel-associated IEC-EC with CAR T cell-positive (CAR^+) infiltration in 158 cilta-cel-treated patients at MD Anderson Cancer Center (incidence of 5.1% at a 6-month landmark and 5.7% globally). Cilta-cel infiltration was the primary cause of IEC-EC, and all cases demonstrated monoclonal or oligoclonal T cell populations as measured by vector integration analysis, flow cytometry and T cell receptor sequencing. Patients with IEC-EC had 100-fold more CAR T cell persistence in the peripheral blood than patients without IEC-EC. RNA sequencing analysis revealed increased cytotoxic and inflammatory programs associated with the CAR^+ infiltrates relative to controls. Clonal vector integration occurred in introns of highly expressed genes without evidence of vector-mediated mutagenesis. Candidate driver mutations were sparse and heterogeneous, distinguishing IEC-EC from peripheral T cell lymphoma following CAR T cell therapy. In sum, we find that IEC-EC pathology represents a distinct, duodenum-predominant, clonal lymphoproliferative disorder characterized by the infiltration of clonal CAR^+ cytotoxic T cells into the gastrointestinal tract. Multimodal profiling of patients with biopsy-confirmed immune effector cell-associated enterocolitis following ciltacabtagene autoleucel shows that CAR T cell infiltrates are concentrated in the duodenum and have a more cytotoxic and clonal phenotype with loss of resident T cells, suggesting that this is a lymphoproliferative disorder with neoplastic characteristics.

title: AI-Driven Analysis of Patient-Derived Models.
source: PubMed · Methods in molecular biology (Clifton, N.J.)
desc: [Methods in molecular biology (Clifton, N.J.)] As a crucial component in preclinical cancer research, patient-derived models (PDMs) are experiencing a substantial transformation due to AI integration. AI improves the conversion efficiency of PDMs' static-dynamic predictions through cross-modal data integration and supports a comprehensive precision medicine technology platform that encompasses everything from molecular mechanisms to clinical translation. In clinical translation, the "AI-PDMs" system is revolutionizing oncology drug development and enabling personalized treatment decisions, moving from experience-based methods to data-driven strategies. This paper provides a detailed summary of AI's innovative uses of PDMs, such as machine learning-based high-dimensional pharmacological sensitivity data mining, deep learning-enhanced 3D tumor microenvironment modeling, and computer vision-driven advancements in pathological feature annotation, thereby offering a systematic framework for future cancer diagnosis and treatment innovations.

title: The Effect of AI-Powered Chatbot Simulator-Based Climate-Resilient Perinatal Care Training on Midwifery Students' Climate Change Knowledge, Awareness, and Risk Assessment Skills
desc: [Newly registered clinical trial, no results yet; sponsor: Büşra HIZLIOL; conditions: Climate-Resilient Perinatal Care Education; type: INTERVENTIONAL; phase: NA; enrollment: 88; status: NOT_YET_RECRUITING] Climate change poses significant risks to maternal, fetal, and neonatal health through environmental hazards such as extreme heat, air pollution, and climate-related disasters. Midwives play a crucial role in identifying these risks, providing preventive counseling, and promoting climate-resilient perinatal care. Integrating artificial intelligence (AI)-supported simulation into midwifery education may enhance students' knowledge, climate change awareness, and clinical risk assessment skills. This study aims to evaluate the effect of climate-resilient perinatal care training supported by an AI-powered chatbot simulator on midwifery students' climate change knowledge, awareness, and climate-related perinatal risk assessment skills. The study is designed as a randomized controlled trial with pretest, posttest, and four-week follow-up assessments. A total of 88 third- and fourth-year midwifery students at the University of Health Sciences, Hamidiye Faculty of Health Sciences, Türkiye, will be allocated to an intervention group (n=44) or a control group (n=44) using stratified randomization based on academic year and grade point average. Both groups will receive a four-week climate-resilient perinatal care education program consisting of eight hours of face-to-face training. Following the educational program, the intervention group will participate in AI-powered chatbot-based clinical simulations involving climate-related perinatal health scenarios, while the control group will receive an educational brochure. Climate-resilient perinatal care knowledge and climate change awareness will be assessed in both groups at baseline, immediately after the intervention, and at a four-week follow-up. Climate-related perinatal risk assessment skills will additionally be evaluated in the intervention group at posttest and follow-up using a structured observational assessment tool. The findings are expected to provide evidence regarding the effectiveness of AI-supported simulation in climate-resilient midwifery education.

title: An LLM-assisted Pipeline for Identifying ClinicalTrials.gov Registry Changes and Their Association with Primary Endpoint Positivity
desc: Registration of randomized clinical trials (RCTs) in a public registry such as ClinicalTrials.gov should minimize the risk of reporting bias. However, records may be modified during a trial and the resulting discrepancies are not always apparent without a detailed examination of all version histories, a process that is cumbersome when performed manually. We developed an automated workflow to investigate whether specific changes to RCT registry entries are associated with primary endpoint positivity. Our pipeline extracts RCT records from ClinicalTrials.gov and systematically detects changes between successive versions using a combination of deterministic textual analysis and large language model (LLM)-assisted classification. We could show a positive association between trial positivity and changes to primary outcomes (OR 1.91; 95% CI 1.48-2.47) as well as to arms and interventions (OR 2.10; 95% CI 1.62-2.73). Associations were weaker when changes occurred exclusively before the primary completion date, pointing to the importance of timing in evaluating potentially consequential modifications to RCT design. Our automated pipeline can enable analysis of trial registration records at scale, facilitating the work of reviewers and meta-scientists to promote research integrity.

title: Machine Learning-Assisted Raman Spectroscopy for Quantitative Prediction of Multicomponent Mixtures
desc: Machine Learning (ML)-assisted Raman spectroscopy that can efficiently analyze molecularly specific fingerprints is well suited for quantitative analysis of complex chemical mixtures. However, developing accurate predictive ML models for multicomponent systems remains difficult because collecting sufficient experimental calibration data is slow, expensive, and limited. In this work, we present a ML-assisted Raman spectroscopy framework for predicting the quantitative composition of multicomponent lipid mixtures (consisting of 15 lipids). To reduce the experimental burden of generating extensive multicomponent spectral datasets, we computationally constructed a large spectral library using experimentally measured pure-component Raman spectra from 15 lipids, including triglycerides, medium- and long-chain fatty acids, and fatty acid methyl and ethyl esters. Mixture compositions were sampled across a constrained compositional space and used to generate training spectra from weighted combinations of the pure component spectra. Experimentally prepared mixtures were then used to evaluate the model under real measurement conditions. To reduce the mismatch between library-generated spectra and experimental mixture spectra, a linear correction strategy was applied to account for systematic spectral differences caused by mixing effects, intermolecular interactions, and measurement variability. The corrected experimental spectra were then used for concentration prediction with an uncertainty-aware workflow. The compositions of the 15 lipid mixtures were successfully predicted using the ML model trained solely on a simulated dataset, achieving R^2 values exceeding 0.95 for each lipid. By combining scalable, library-based model training with experimental validation on physical multicomponent mixtures, this approach minimizes the need for exhaustive calibration datasets while maintaining high quantitative accuracy. The proposed framework offers a practical path for quantitative Raman analysis of chemical mixtures and can easily be extended to quality control applications across the food, pharmaceutical, nutraceutical, and chemical industries.

title: Future Directions for Precision Medicine in the Age of AI.
source: PubMed · Methods in molecular biology (Clifton, N.J.)
desc: [Methods in molecular biology (Clifton, N.J.)] Precision medicine, which involves tailoring medical treatment to the individual characteristics of each patient, is poised for a new era of advancement through artificial intelligence (AI). This chapter explores the future directions of precision medicine in the context of AI-driven innovation, focusing on emerging technologies and their impact on personalized care. We discuss recent breakthroughs in AI-enabled diagnostics, genomics, drug discovery, and clinical decision-making, highlighting how these developments are reshaping the practice of medicine. We also examine the challenges and opportunities in implementing AI for precision medicine, including data integration, model interpretability, regulatory considerations, and ethical issues. Drawing on high-impact research and reports from leading institutions, we present a forward-looking analysis of how AI will drive the next generation of personalized treatments. The convergence of AI and precision medicine promises to revolutionize healthcare by improving early disease detection, optimizing therapy selection, and enabling truly individualized patient care.

title: THE EFFECT OF AI-SUPPORTED WOMEN'S HEALTH NURSING DIAGNOSTIC SYSTEMS ON NURSES' DIAGNOSTIC PERCEPTIONS AND AI ATTITUDES
desc: [Newly registered clinical trial, no results yet; sponsor: Ardahan University; conditions: Artificial Intelligence (AI), Nurse Based Care Management, Nurse Led Intervention; type: INTERVENTIONAL; phase: NA; enrollment: 60; status: NOT_YET_RECRUITING] This research is planned to determine the effect of an AI-assisted nursing diagnostic system on nurses' perceptions of diagnoses, their opinions regarding diagnoses, and their attitudes towards artificial intelligence. The research will be conducted using a randomized controlled experimental design with an AI-assisted nursing diagnostic system developed for the field of women's health and obstetrics. The study population consists of nurses working in the obstetrics and gynecology departments (delivery room, postpartum ward, etc.) of two hospitals and providing care to women aged 18-49. Approximately 600 nurses meeting the inclusion criteria were identified as constituting the population. In the study, nurses' perceptions of diagnoses, their opinions regarding nursing diagnoses, and their attitudes towards artificial intelligence will be evaluated through structured data collection tools. The use of the AI-assisted system will be compared with traditional nursing diagnostic processes to analyze the system's impact on clinical decision-making processes. The study expects that the AI-assisted nursing diagnostic system will increase diagnostic accuracy, support clinical decision-making processes, and positively influence nurses' attitudes towards technology. Furthermore, it is anticipated that the findings will contribute to the standardization of nursing care and provide a scientific basis for the development of digital health applications aimed at improving maternal and infant safety in the field of women's health.

title: WakeSentry: real-time awakening detection from single-channel EEG across sleep cohorts and forehead headbands
desc: Objective/Background: Awakenings after sleep onset are a core measure of sleep continuity, and EEG headbands and closed-loop stimulators, now used at home, must detect each one as it happens, to count it or to stop stimulation. Open sleep stagers match expert scorers, yet have been evaluated only offline over whole nights, so their real-time performance is untested. Patients/Methods: To fill this gap, we developed WakeSentry, which reads only past frontal EEG and learns the moment of waking through an awakening module. We tested it on 1,529 nights from five polysomnography (PSG) cohorts, three clinical, each held out of training, and on 224 headband nights, against GSSC, U-Sleep and YASA. Results: At a matched rate of 0.5 false awakenings per hour, WakeSentry caught more awakenings than GSSC in every cohort and on both headbands. On PSG its sensitivity rose from 63.8% to 70.5%, above U-Sleep and YASA on average. On the headbands it rose from 49.8% to 53.9%, a gain lost without the awakening module. With thresholds preset on the training cohorts, it still outperformed GSSC in six of seven test sets, with at most 0.40 false awakenings per hour. As a replayed stimulator gate, it shortened stimulation during wake in five test sets while staying open for at least 85% of N2 and N3. Conclusions: WakeSentry therefore works in patients and on unseen headbands. It can count awakenings at home and stop stimulation at each one, enabling multi-night monitoring of insomnia and closed-loop stimulation that stops when the sleeper wakes.

title: Analyzing Electronic Health Records for Precision Medicine.
source: PubMed · Methods in molecular biology (Clifton, N.J.)
desc: [Methods in molecular biology (Clifton, N.J.)] Precision medicine relies heavily on electronic health records (EHRs) to systematically capture longitudinal clinical data across populations. Integrating omics data, such as genomics, proteomics, and metabolomics, with EHRs holds transformative potential for individual-level disease risk assessment and therapeutic optimization. Recent advances in artificial intelligence, particularly multimodal learning algorithms, have enabled deeper exploration of EHR data, enhancing predictive modeling, patient stratification, and phenotyping. These artificial intelligence (AI)-driven approaches are expanding the scope of precision medicine from research contexts to scalable, real-time clinical decision-making. In real-world implementation, however, leveraging EHRs for precision medicine demands navigating complex technical, ethical, and operational challenges. These include data interoperability, model generalizability, and equity concerns. Future efforts should emphasize standardization, responsible AI practices, and integration of digital health and patient-reported outcomes to build learning health systems that are adaptive, equitable, and clinically impactful.

title: Machine Learning Prediction of ADHD in Adolescents: Gaming, Sleep, and Sport
desc: [Newly registered clinical trial, no results yet; sponsor: Yalin Aygun; conditions: Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD); type: OBSERVATIONAL; enrollment: 750; status: NOT_YET_RECRUITING] ADHD is one of the most common mental health conditions in teenagers. It can affect school performance, friendships, and overall well-being. Some everyday habits and lifestyle factors-how much a teenager plays internet games, how well they sleep, and whether they take part in sports-have each been linked to ADHD symptoms. However, these three factors have almost always been studied one at a time, and no study has yet tested whether looking at them together can help predict which teenagers have more severe ADHD symptoms. This study aims to find out whether internet gaming, sleep quality, and sport participation, when considered together, can predict ADHD symptom severity in adolescents aged 12-17. We will invite 750 teenagers from secondary schools in Malatya, Türkiye, to complete a set of short, anonymous questionnaires about their attention and hyperactivity symptoms, gaming habits, sleep, and sport participation. We will then use machine learning-a type of computer analysis that can detect complex patterns and interactions between many factors at once-to build and test a prediction model. The main question this study seeks to answer is: Do internet gaming, sleep quality, and sport participation jointly carry information that helps predict ADHD symptoms in teenagers, beyond what is already known from basic characteristics such as age, sex, and socioeconomic status? We are not testing a treatment, and the study does not involve any medication, biological samples, or changes to participants' usual routines. The findings may help schools, families, and health professionals identify teenagers who could benefit from early support and from healthier lifestyle habits. This is an exploratory study; it cannot show cause and effect, and any prediction model would need to be tested in other groups before being used in practice.

title: RadMatch: Auditable Radiology Report Evaluation via Finding-Level Matching
desc: As AI systems are increasingly used to draft radiology reports, reliably evaluating their clinical quality remains a critical challenge. It extracts findings from a reference and a candidate report, matches them by clinical equivalence, grades each match over ten clinical attributes, and gives every match and unmatched finding a verdict and a clinical-significance tier. To validate metrics on CT, we build and release MetricEval-BodyCT, the first public metric-evaluation benchmark of chest and abdomen CT reports annotated by radiologists error by error. title: The Shrinking Grace Period and the Downsizing of Ransomware Victims: Exploitation Timelines and Breach Size Among US Health Care Providers, 2016-2026
desc: Objectives: To examine how quickly software vulnerabilities are exploited after public disclosure, and whether hacking breaches at US health care providers changed in size after 2021, a period in which earlier studies had found attacks concentrating on large organizations. Methods: Retrospective analysis of public data. We linked the CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog (1,748 entries) with CVE publication dates to measure time to confirmed exploitation by half-year of publication (2021-2025). We also analyzed 8,029 breach reports submitted to the HHS Office for Civil Rights, focusing on hacking/IT incidents at health care providers. Results: Median time to confirmed exploitation was 24 days for vulnerabilities published from late 2021 to mid 2022, 0 days for those published in the second half of 2022, and 6 days in 2023-2025, with no further shortening across 2023-2025 (P = .40). About a quarter were exploited on or before the day of disclosure. Among provider hacking breaches, the share affecting fewer than 5,000 people fell from 42% in 2016 to 32% in 2022 (trend P = .004) and rose to 46% in 2025 (P < .001). Conclusions: The window between disclosure and exploitation had narrowed to about a week before generative AI was widely available. After 2022, breaches moved toward smaller events, reversing the earlier concentration on large organizations. Defenses that depend on patching speed will not protect small providers.

title: Artificial intelligence for detecting and predicting glaucomatous progression.
desc: [Current opinion in ophthalmology] This review examines the current state of artificial intelligence (AI) models for the detection and prediction of glaucomatous progression. Machine learning and deep learning models have been developed to analyze longitudinal data from optic disc photographs, optical coherence tomography images, and visual field tests to identify worsening glaucoma. Recent AI research has also expanded beyond simply detecting progression to predicting future disease trajectories. These approaches may provide more efficient assessment than clinician review alone. AI models can rapidly analyze large volumes of clinical data to support individualized glaucoma management; these models can guide treatment intensity and follow-up intervals by detecting and predicting glaucomatous progression. However, significant hurdles to clinical adoption remain, including the "black box" nature of AI, absence of a universally accepted reference standard for progression, variable data quality, and limited generalizability across populations and clinical settings. AI is poised to function as a clinical decision support tool rather than a replacement for clinicians. Prospective studies are needed to determine the impact of AI in improving patient outcomes, clinical efficiency, and healthcare costs.

title: Prediction of Post-Spinal Hypotension During Cesarean Delivery Using Machine Learning Algorithms

The primary outcome is post-spinal hypotension, defined as a decrease in systolic blood pressure of at least 20% from baseline and/or the requirement for vasopressor administration within the first 15 minutes after spinal anesthesia. The best-performing model will be evaluated in the independent prospective cohort to assess its predictive performance in a real clinical setting.

Digital Twin Models for Cancer.
source: PubMed · Methods in molecular biology (Clifton, N.J.)
desc: [Methods in molecular biology (Clifton, N.J.)] The inherent complexity and heterogeneity of cancer create an urgent need for individualized treatment strategies. However, traditional population-based medical approaches have limitations in addressing patient-specific differences. Meanwhile, conventional clinical trials are often constrained by lengthy timelines, high costs, and difficulties in patient recruitment, particularly for rare cancers and pediatric populations, thereby hindering the development of novel therapies. To address these challenges, medical digital twins (MDTs) have emerged as dynamic computational models that represent an individual patient's physiology and disease state and are continuously updated as real-world data accumulate. To explain how MDTs transform accumulating patient data into actionable insights, this chapter first introduces their fundamental architecture, comprising five interdependent components: the patient, data connection, patient-in-silico, interface, and twin synchronization. Within this architecture, the patient-in-silico component can be constructed using mechanistic models based on established biological principles, artificial intelligence models driven by large-scale clinical data, or hybrid models combining both approaches. Representative mechanistic and artificial intelligence-driven MDTs are then presented to illustrate how these modeling approaches have been applied in oncology. Specifically, MDTs can support precision oncology and improve the efficiency of clinical trials. In precision oncology, MDTs can simulate disease progression and therapeutic responses, allowing treatment regimens to be tested virtually before administration and thereby supporting personalized treatment decisions. In virtual clinical trials, MDTs can enhance randomized trials through the PROCOVA™ methodology, provide synthetic control arms for single-arm studies, and support the identification of optimal dosing regimens in early-phase trials. However, MDTs also face challenges related to computational complexity, generalizability across diverse populations, AI-related model validation and regulatory compliance, and underdeveloped ethical frameworks for continuous-learning systems. Despite these challenges, MDTs hold considerable potential to reshape cancer care, optimize individualized therapies, and accelerate oncology drug development.

title: Adolescent Self-Esteem, Temperament, Emotion Regulation, and Sport Participation
desc: [Newly registered clinical trial, no results yet; sponsor: Inonu University; conditions: Global Self-Esteem in Adolescents; type: OBSERVATIONAL; enrollment: 500; status: NOT_YET_RECRUITING] This observational study aims to examine how temperament, emotion regulation, and sport participation are related to global self-esteem in adolescents. Participants will complete questionnaires measuring temperament, cognitive reappraisal, expressive suppression, and global self-esteem. Information about sport participation, including participation status, sport type, weekly training hours, years of participation, and competition level, will also be collected. Demographic characteristics such as age and gender will be considered in the analyses. The researchers will use statistical and machine learning methods to determine how well these characteristics predict global self-esteem. The study will also examine whether nonlinear relationships and combinations of characteristics improve prediction compared with a standard linear model, and which characteristics contribute most strongly to prediction. Differences between adolescents who participate in sports and those who do not will also be explored. This study is observational. Participants will not be assigned to a sport program, treatment, or other intervention. Because the data will be collected at one point in time, the findings will describe associations and predictive relationships and will not establish cause and effect.

Individual Treatment Effect Estimation Based on AI.
source: PubMed · Methods in molecular biology (Clifton, N.J.)
desc: [Methods in molecular biology (Clifton, N.J.)] The rapid growth of electronic health records, clinical trial repositories, and real-world medical data creates new opportunities for estimating how treatment effects vary across patients. In recent years, a wide range of artificial intelligence (AI)-based methods has been developed to move beyond average treatment effects (ATE) and support more individualized treatment decisions. However, despite this methodological progress, only a small number of these approaches are used in routine clinical practice. At the same time, precision medicine highlights the limitations of relying solely on population-average treatment effects. In this chapter, we review the main ideas and methods underlying AI-based individual treatment effect (ITE) estimation. We discuss the limitations of conventional subgroup analysis and introduce the major classes of conditional average treatment effect (CATE) estimation methods, including outcome modeling, effect modeling, and deep causal learning approaches. We further illustrate their use in both randomized trials and observational studies, with examples from intensive blood pressure control and sepsis care, and highlight the evaluation and interpretability challenges essential for clinical translation.

desc: Real-world clinical diagnosis is a complex process in which the doctor is required to obtain information from both interaction with the patient and conducting medical exams. Additionally, the doctor needs to adapt to different patient personas, as well as noisy and incomplete information that can happen at any time during the process. title: AI-Driven Approaches in Pharmacogenomics for Precision Medicine.
source: PubMed · Methods in molecular biology (Clifton, N.J.)
desc: [Methods in molecular biology (Clifton, N.J.)] With the advancement of precision medicine, pharmacogenomics (PGx) is playing an increasingly important role in guiding personalized drug therapy. The rapid development of artificial intelligence (AI) technologies, particularly machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL), is infusing new momentum into PGx research and significantly accelerating its translational applications in clinical settings. This review systematically summarizes recent progress and practical applications of AI in the field of PGx. We highlight that AI not only enhances the interpretation of complex genetic variations but also uncovers potential mechanisms of drug response and adverse reactions from large-scale heterogeneous data, thereby exerting substantial influence on both drug development and clinical pharmacotherapy. Nevertheless, the clinical implementation of AI in PGx still faces multiple challenges, including data bias, limited model generalizability, insufficient regulatory frameworks, and ethical and legal concerns. In the future, with continued optimization of algorithms, interdisciplinary collaboration, and the establishment of robust ethical standards, AI is expected to play a more central role in advancing personalized medicine and bridging the gap between research and clinical practice.

desc: Hospital quality improvement (QI) programs generally proceed in two stages: (1) hypothesis generation, which identifies candidate factors that may improve care quality and efficiency, and (2) confirmatory analyses, which implement and evaluate QI initiatives targeting these factors. Although most research focuses on the confirmatory stage, hypothesis generation is equally important because it shapes where teams focus their effort. Currently, hypothesis generation depends on expert-driven, qualitative methods (e.g., Lean Healthcare tools) that can be anecdotal, hard to reproduce, time-consuming, and resource-intensive. title: Artificial Intelligence and Deep Learning Approaches in Genome-Wide Association Studies.
source: PubMed · Methods in molecular biology (Clifton, N.J.)
desc: [Methods in molecular biology (Clifton, N.J.)] Genome-wide association studies (GWAS) have been instrumental in uncovering the genetic basis of complex traits, yet classical single-variant testing remains limited in power and biological interpretability. Over the past decade, GWAS methodology has expanded from purely statistical association frameworks toward integrative models that incorporate functional annotations, multi-trait information, and data-driven prioritization strategies. Early developments leveraged regulatory genomics and cross-phenotype statistics to improve locus discovery, while machine learning approaches enabled systematic ranking of sub-threshold variants. More recently, deep learning architectures, including Transformer-based frameworks, have been introduced to integrate GWAS summary signals with linkage disequilibrium patterns and diverse genomic annotations. In parallel, multi-omics integration and transfer learning across related traits have emerged as practical solutions for limited sample sizes and population heterogeneity. This chapter reviews the evolving methodological landscape of AI-enabled GWAS, highlights key advances in variant discovery and functional interpretation, and discusses remaining challenges such as ancestry bias, interpretability, and the need for biological validation. Together, these approaches provide a foundation for more context-aware and scalable genetic studies of complex disease.

title: Advanced Flexible Wearables for Next-Generation Digital Healthcare.
source: PubMed · Methods in molecular biology (Clifton, N.J.)
desc: [Methods in molecular biology (Clifton, N.J.)] The growing emphasis on personalized medicine is accelerating the shift toward precision healthcare, demanding real-time, high-frequency physiological data acquisition through minimally invasive or noninvasive means. Flexible wearable electronics have emerged as a transformative solution, overcoming the limitations of conventional rigid medical devices. By integrating highly compliant materials with miniaturized systems, these platforms enable continuous, stable, and comfortable monitoring of multimodal physiological signals such as electrocardiograms (ECG), body temperature, blood pressure, and sweat biomarkers. This chapter explores cutting-edge advances in flexible wearable technology, such as electronic skin with sweat management, implantable bioresorbable microneedles (IBMN), self-powered haptic interfaces, and deep learning-enhanced biosignal processing. We analyze the role of these innovations in advancing intelligent, patient-centric digital healthcare while addressing challenges in clinical translation and scalability.

desc: The curation of large cohort datasets for developing deep learning models demands annotating or editing over the AI-predicted labels. title: Artificial intelligence in basic and translational cardiovascular research.
desc: [Biomedicine & pharmacotherapy = Biomedecine & pharmacotherapie] Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly used in cardiovascular research where conventional analysis struggles with scale, heterogeneity, and multimodal integration. Its contribution differs across imaging, computational omics, mechanistic simulation, and drug discovery. This narrative review examines substantive applications of machine learning and deep learning while distinguishing them from routine bioinformatics and purely biophysical modeling. We assess independent biological units, validation strategies, and strength of inference in representative studies. Deep-learning imaging systems can provide reproducible quantitative phenotypes, but workflow performance alone does not establish mechanism. In single-cell and spatial studies, clustering, integration, trajectory inference, and network reconstruction generally yield associations or hypotheses unless experimentally supported. Mechanistic interpretation is bounded by the specific effect established through targeted perturbation or rescue with functional testing; lineage tracing and orthogonal readouts provide complementary support, not standalone proof of causation. Hybrid AI-biophysical models may accelerate personalized simulation, whereas heart-on-chip, engineered tissue, and organoid systems without learned components are validation platforms rather than AI methods. In drug discovery, active learning and molecular redesign can prioritize candidates, but predicted reductions in ion-channel liability do not demonstrate biological safety or reduced proarrhythmic risk. Major limitations include pseudoreplication, data leakage, domain shift, batch effects, uncertain labels, few independent hearts, demographic imbalance, incomplete calibration, and limited transfer among animal, iPSC-derived, and adult human systems. AI is most valuable when it produces robust phenotypes or experimentally testable hypotheses within a transparent validation framework, rather than when predictive accuracy is treated as mechanistic evidence.

Despite its importance for preoperative staging and surgical planning, computational VI assessment remains underexplored. Two major challenges are the lack of public datasets and the diagnostic ambiguity at the tumor-vessel interface, which leads to substantial inter-rater variability even among expert radiologists. To address these limitations, we introduce the CURVAS-PDACVI Dataset and Challenge, an open benchmark for uncertainty-aware AI in PDAC staging based on a densely annotated dataset with five independent expert annotations per scan. title: AI-Driven Monitoring of Biomechanical Loading in Mild Traumatic Brain Injury.
source: PubMed · Methods in molecular biology (Clifton, N.J.)
desc: [Methods in molecular biology (Clifton, N.J.)] Mild traumatic brain injury (mTBI) is difficult to identify rapidly because clinical symptoms may be delayed and conventional CT or MRI often reveals no structural abnormalities. Biomechanics-based monitoring provides an objective complementary strategy by measuring head kinematics at the moment of impact and estimating the resulting brain deformation. This review summarizes how artificial intelligence (AI) can overcome two major barriers to this approach: errors in wearable-sensor measurements and the high computational cost of finite element head models. AI-based methods can denoise instrumented mouthguard signals, distinguish true impacts from false triggers, and infer impact direction, location, speed, and force. Deep learning head models can further map six-degree-of-freedom head kinematics to whole-brain strain and strain-rate distributions within milliseconds, enabling near-real-time tissue-level injury assessment. Recent advances, including kinematic feature optimization, principal component analysis, impact subtyping, transfer learning, unsupervised domain adaptation, and spatiotemporal prediction, have improved model efficiency, interpretability, and generalizability across impact scenarios. Integrating wearable sensing with AI-accelerated brain modeling could support rapid removal from exposure, earlier clinical evaluation and intervention, and monitoring of cumulative impact dose. Future research should improve sensor wearability and coupling, incorporate subject-specific brain morphology and cortical folding, represent cerebrospinal fluid mechanics more realistically, and develop unified models that jointly estimate brain deformation and predict clinically confirmed injury. AI-enabled biomechanical monitoring may therefore complement symptom- and imaging-based assessments and advance real-time, personalized mTBI detection and prevention.

title: How Well Do Segmentation Foundation Models Generalize Across Structural and Functional Medical Imaging?
desc: Segmentation foundation models offer reusable tools for universal medical-image segmentation, but their development and evaluation have largely centered on structural CT and MRI imaging. Functional imaging such as PET provides complementary metabolic information yet remains less studied and validated. Moreover, existing evaluations often involve different datasets and tasks, making modality-associated variation difficult to distinguish from differences in segmentation targets and data distributions. To enable a more direct comparison, we introduce UMD, a whole-body multi-organ dataset comprising 490 PET/CT and 464 PET/MRI examinations with 13 annotated organs (approximately 675,000 2D slices and 12,000 3D organ annotations). title: Computed Tomography-Derived Machine Learning for Risk Assessment in Aortic Dissection: A Narrative Review.
desc: [Heart failure clinics] Machine learning (ML) has emerged as a promising tool for improving diagnosis and prognostic assessment across a wide spectrum of cardiovascular diseases. A literature search was conducted in PubMed and Embase to identify relevant studies focusing on ML approaches to computed tomography (CT)-based risk stratification in aortic dissection. ML-based analysis of CT imaging offers significant potential to enhance prognostic assessment and risk stratification in aortic dissection. By integrating imaging, clinical, and biomarker data, these approaches may enable earlier identification of high-risk patients and support more personalized management strategies.

title: Why ML-based cough models do not generalize: a systematic cross-dataset evaluation for tuberculosis screening
desc: Cough acoustics are promising for non-invasive tuberculosis (TB) screening, yet whether machine learning (ML) models capture disease-related acoustics or artifacts of data collection remains unresolved. We evaluated the cross-dataset generalizability of classical ML and deep learning (DL) cough-based TB classifiers across three independent datasets. Despite moderate within-dataset performance (ROC-AUC up to $0.76 \pm 0.06$), both pipelines fail to generalize, with external performance frequently below 0.6, indicating a possible limitation of the data. We further observed that audio representations are organized by recording device and dataset rather than TB status, predicted TB probability tracks country-level prevalence in CODA, and device mismatch degrades transfer while device-diverse training improves it. title: Statistical Design, Inference, and Trustworthy Medical AI.
source: PubMed · Methods in molecular biology (Clifton, N.J.)
desc: [Methods in molecular biology (Clifton, N.J.)] In the rapidly evolving field of artificial intelligence (AI), statistics plays a crucial role in addressing challenges faced by medical AI. This review begins by highlighting the primary tasks of medical AI and the integration of statistical methodologies into their modeling processes. Despite the widespread application of AI in medicine and healthcare, key challenges persist: poor model interpretability, lack of causal reasoning, overfitting, unfairness, imbalanced datasets, AI "hallucinations" and "disinformation." Statistics provides unique strategies to tackle these challenges, including rigorous statistical design, regularization techniques, and statistical frameworks grounded in causal inference. Finally, the review offers several recommendations for the sustainable development of medical AI: enhancing data quality, promoting model simplicity and transparency, fostering independent validation standards, and facilitating interdisciplinary collaboration between statisticians and medical AI practitioners.

title: FLARE: A Full-Lifecycle Dense Supervision Paradigm for Long-Horizon Coding Agents via Generative Reward Model
desc: While test-time scaling enhances Large Language Model (LLM) agents in long-horizon software engineering (SWE), sparse binary rewards (Pass/Fail) create a severe credit assignment crisis and waste failed exploratory trajectories. Current trajectory optimization and scaling methods are costly and structurally limited, relying on heuristic state reuse without causal diagnosis or delayed scalar scoring without actionable online guidance. We propose FLARE (Full-Lifecycle Alignment and Reward Engine), a novel dense supervision paradigm driven by a lightweight Generative Reward Model (GRM). First, RADAR, an offline causal-aware diagnostic framework, extracts high-fidelity, hindsight-free supervision through causal-chain backtracking to distill a GRM providing real-time, step-level risk feedback. title: AI-empowered lipidomics advances metabolic research.
source: PubMed · Trends in endocrinology and metabolism: TEM
desc: [Trends in endocrinology and metabolism: TEM] The complex structures and dynamic processes of lipids make it challenging to decipher lipid reprogramming in metabolic diseases. Integrating artificial intelligence (AI) with lipidomics, mass spectrometry imaging, and lipid metabolic fluxomics enables rapid, high-precision, and in-depth spatiotemporal profiling of lipid species. In this review, we summarize advances in AI-empowered lipidomics, which not only accelerate spatiotemporal data processing but also offer new avenues to resolve the heterogeneity of lipid metabolism. Importantly, AI-assisted lipidomics could identify candidate biomarkers and generate testable hypotheses about disease mechanisms. Furthermore, we evaluate whether computational advances yield trustworthy evidence by examining annotation confidence, quantitative accuracy, cross-platform reproducibility, uncertainty calibration, and external validation. We also address the current limitations of AI-assisted lipidomics, particularly the risk of AI hallucinations.

title: Co-Pilot for Health: Personalized Algorithmic AI Nudging to Improve Health Outcomes
desc: The ability to shape health behaviors of large populations automatically, across wearable types and disease conditions at scale has tremendous potential to improve global health outcomes. We designed and implemented an AI driven platform for digital algorithmic nudging, enabled by a Graph-Neural Network (GNN) based Recommendation System, and granular health behavior data from wearable fitness devices. Here we describe the efficacy results of this platform with its capabilities of personalized and contextual nudging to $n=84,764$ individuals over a 12-week period in Singapore. We statistically validated that participants in the target group who received such AI optimized daily nudges increased daily physical activity like step count by 6.17% ($p = 3.09\times10^{-4}$) and weekly minutes of Moderate to Vigorous Physical Activity (MVPA) by 7.61% ($p = 1.16\times10^{-2}$), compared to matched

title: The scientific record is never finished.
desc: [Science (New York, N.Y.)] The scholarly scientific record has always been a work in progress. From the earliest days of scientific publishing, new findings would come along that changed the way earlier findings are understood. When research journals were published only in print, occasional errors would be reported by the authors or found by others, and papers would be retracted or corrected. When publishing became digital, many more people could quickly access and scrutinize data and images for accuracy. Now, in the age of artificial intelligence (AI), it is possible for machines to do these examinations more expeditiously and at a larger scale. All of this has added an important new layer to the publishing process and put more responsibility on authors, who must update their work if new issues arise. In response to this need, Science is improving the ways in which it will flag and notate papers that require adjustment or where changes are under consideration. Our Editorial Policies now reflect these updates.

title: Tracking Representations in LLM Reasoning Traces for Iterated Games
desc: Large language model (LLM) agents achieve state-of-the-art performance across domains through chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning. Despite their ubiquitous use, little is understood about the relationship between the externalized trace and the model's actual computation. We address this by investigating how LLM agents make decisions in iterative games with incomplete information. Using a series of mechanistic interpretability techniques, we find that the model forms and iteratively revises an internal representation of the game throughout the CoT. Once the model prematurely commits to an incorrect belief, it rarely recovers. This failure is manifested in both the literal trace and the layer activations. title: Prediction of Human-Virus Protein-Protein Interactions.
source: PubMed · Methods in molecular biology (Clifton, N.J.)
desc: [Methods in molecular biology (Clifton, N.J.)] Human-Virus Protein-Protein Interactions (HV-PPIs) are the core mechanisms underlying viral invasion of host cells, completion of the viral life cycle, and induction of pathological responses. Predicting HV-PPIs in higher accuracy is of great significance for elucidating viral pathogenic mechanisms, developing antiviral drugs, and designing vaccines. However, traditional experimental methods such as Yeast Two-Hybrid (Y2H) and Affinity Purification-Mass Spectrometry (AP-MS) face bottlenecks including low throughput, high cost, high false positive rates, and incomplete data in the identification of cross-species interactions. In recent years, computational biology approaches, especially deep learning-based multimodal fusion frameworks, have emerged as the primary driving force for accelerating HV-PPIs prediction. This review systematically summarizes the latest advances in the field of HV-PPIs prediction, elaborates on key aspects such as data construction, feature engineering, deep learning architectures, and performance evaluation, summarizes the technical essentials, advantages, and limitations of existing methods, discusses the development trends of the field by integrating representative research findings from recent years, and serves as a reference for future investigations in this domain.

title: Why Trust Your Agent? Empirical Security Gains from TRiSM-Guided Agentic Workflows in Healthcare
desc: Agent-based AI has enabled the automation of tasks by exposing application tools and resources to large language models (LLMs). However, to improve scope and accuracy, agents are often given access rights that exceed those of ordinary users, introducing significant security risks and potential regulatory breaches. This paper applies the AI Trust, Risk, and Security Management (TRiSM) framework to a medical report-generation application to demonstrate how an insecure baseline workflow can be transformed into a security-conscious agentic workflow. Both designs were evaluated with five LLMs (Claude Haiku 4.5, GPT-4.1-nano, GPT-4.1-mini, GPT-5.4-mini and Gemini 2.5 Flash) across 800 report generations and 500 attack trials covering RAG poisoning, data-field injection and client-side network injection. title: Technology-Enabled Skin Longevity Optimization.
desc: [Facial plastic surgery : FPS] Aims and Backgrounds: Facial aging is a multifactorial process involving cellular senescence, ultraviolet damage, and structural decline across the epidermis, dermis, subcutaneous fat, and superficial musculoaponeurotic system. Contemporary rejuvenation has evolved beyond surgical repositioning toward biologically targeted cutaneous optimization. Energy-based technologies including laser photothermolysis, radiofrequency-mediated dermal thermomodulation, microfocused ultrasound, and emerging microwave and cryobiologic modalities induce controlled tissue injury that activates wound-healing pathways, fibroblast proliferation, and extracellular matrix remodeling. Regenerative strategies including microneedling-assisted mechanotransduction, platelet-derived biologics, autologous fat grafting, collagen biostimulators, and extracellular vesicle therapies provide biologically oriented tissue restoration through paracrine signaling and matrix synthesis. Current and Future Development: Artificial intelligence applications in facial phenotyping, treatment planning, and outcome assessment are emerging. Future directions include senescence-targeting therapies and precision-based multimodal protocols. Multimodal treatment sequencing addressing multiple anatomical layers represents the contemporary standard. Integration of device-based technologies with regenerative adjuncts enables biologically informed, individualized facial rejuvenation.

title: An Explainable and Scalable Hierarchical Tensor Framework for Integrating Multi-Omics and Digital Pathomics
desc: Background: Precision oncology requires integration of heterogeneous molecular and pathology data, yet many fusion models offer limited biologically grounded interpretability and struggle with missing modalities. Methods: We present Hierarchical Interpretable Tensor Fusion (HIT-Fuse), integrating six modalities: somatic copy number variation, DNA methylation, RNA sequencing, microRNA expression, RPPA protein abundance, and vision transformer-derived pathomics across four TCGA cohorts (glioma, lung adenocarcinoma, breast, and kidney cancer). Modality-specific autoencoders compress high-dimensional inputs, followed by two-stage CP tensor decomposition. Missing latent modalities are reconstructed using clinical covariates and observed omics to expand cohorts and retrain downstream models. title: Deep Learning for Protein-Compound Interaction Prediction: Methods and Generalization.
source: PubMed · Methods in molecular biology (Clifton, N.J.)
desc: [Methods in molecular biology (Clifton, N.J.)] Deep learning now underpins most protein-compound interaction (PCI) prediction pipelines, spanning virtual screening, affinity estimation, and lead optimization. Yet strong numbers on standard benchmarks do not reliably translate into discovery outcomes: accuracy can drop sharply under distribution shift, many predictions are hard to rationalize or corroborate with physical evidence, and reported performance is often sensitive to how labels are defined, how data are split, and which metrics are emphasized. In this review, we introduce recent progress in deep learning for PCI prediction across task definitions, protein/ligand representations, interaction modeling architectures, benchmark resources, and evaluation practice, emphasizing the methodological choices that determine reliability outside curated test sets. We relate widely used label and task setups to their underlying assumptions and typical failure modes, analyze how redundancy and similarity leakage can inflate in-distribution results, and highlight recurring trade-offs between model expressiveness, scalability, physical realism, and generalization to unseen targets or chemotypes. We end by outlining practical priorities for evaluation and reporting, including split protocols matched to the intended deployment scenario, explicit treatment of assay heterogeneity, uncertainty-aware and decision-focused metrics, and benchmark designs that better anticipate prospective utility.

title: Multi-institutional grading of Barrett's esophagus dysplasia without stain normalization using a pathology foundation model and multiple instance learning
desc: Barrett's esophagus dysplasia grading suffers substantial inter-observer variability, particularly for low-grade dysplasia, complicating clinical decision-making. We conducted a retrospective multi-institutional diagnostic accuracy study of a foundation model-based deep learning system for dysplasia grading, using 969 H\&E-stained whole slide images from four institutions. Patch-level classifiers trained on expert annotations identified diagnostically relevant regions, followed by attribute-aware multiple instance learning for slide-level classification as non-dysplastic Barrett's esophagus (NDBE), low-grade dysplasia, or high-grade dysplasia. On a held-out test set (n = 130), macro-averaged AUC was 0.96 (95\% CI 0.93--0.98). title: Annual high-resolution mapping reveals warming-driven carbon losses in Spanish forests.
source: PubMed · Ecological applications : a publication of the Ecological Society of America
desc: [Ecological applications : a publication of the Ecological Society of America] Forests play a crucial role as carbon sinks and are central to climate mitigation strategies, yet their long-term provision of this ecosystem service is increasingly uncertain under climate change. Using deep learning techniques on a multisource dataset-combining multispectral satellite data, airborne laser scanning, and ground-based measurements-we produced 10 m resolution annual maps of live woody carbon stocks in mainland Spain from 2017 to 2024. Our analysis revealed substantial live forest carbon losses: Live woody carbon stocks declined by approximately 19% between 2017 and 2024, with the sharpest decline occurring during 2021-2023 following a severe drought in 2022. These losses signal reduced uptake capacity and increased vulnerability to future carbon emissions through decomposition or fire. Conifer forests and Eucalyptus plantations experienced the greatest relative carbon losses, 31% and 37% respectively, while Quercus spp. forests showed high resistance (3% decline) and low-density woodlands and agroforestry systems were the least affected, with live woody carbon stocks declining only approximately 1% in these areas. Our results are consistent with structural overshoot dynamics, where periods of favorable growing conditions promote vegetation growth that subsequently becomes vulnerable during drier conditions. Specifically, high rainfall and cooler summer temperatures were strongly correlated with subsequent carbon losses. These findings reveal a critical challenge for climate policy as forest mitigation potential is hampered by climate change impacts, especially in Mediterranean regions where drought duration and intensity is increasing. This highlights the urgent need to align adaptation and mitigation policies to enhance forest resilience, carbon stock stability, and long-term climate mitigation capacity.

title: A Subspecialty Diagnostic System Powered by Self-Supervised Learning for Cervical Histopathology
desc: Cervical cancer remains a major malignancy in women, with large-scale human papillomavirus-based screening generating a large volume of biopsies and, for advanced cases, surgical specimens, imposing an overwhelming diagnostic burden that necessitates precise histopathological evaluation. Although deep learning shows promise, general foundation models offer a broader reach but remain limited in capturing subspecialty-specific features and task adaptability. We introduce the Cervical Subspecialty Pathology (CerS-Path) diagnostic system, built upon the subspecialized dataset and developed through two synergistic pretraining stages: self-supervised learning on approximately 190 million tissue patches to build a cervical-specific feature extractor, and multimodal enhancement with 2.5 million image-text pairs, followed by diagnostic functions integration and downstream task enhancement. title: Deep learning based numerical approximation algorithms for stochastic partial differential equations.
source: PubMed · Zeitschrift fuer angewandte mathematik und physik
desc: [Zeitschrift fuer angewandte mathematik und physik] In this article, we introduce a deep learning based approximation algorithm for SPDEs. Our approach employs neural networks to approximate the solutions of SPDEs along given realizations of the driving noise process. If applied to a set of simulated noise trajectories, it yields empirical distributions of SPDE solutions, from which functionals like the mean and variance can be estimated. We test the performance of the method on stochastic heat equations with additive and multiplicative noise as well as stochastic Black-Scholes equations with multiplicative noise and Zakai equations from nonlinear filtering theory. In all cases, the proposed algorithm yields accurate results with short runtimes in up to 100 space dimensions.

title: VoxForge: A Unified Foundation Model for Dense 3D Features Across MRI, CT and PET
desc: A unified 3D medical foundation model promises reusable, frozen features that serve a wide variety of tasks such as segmentation, classification and registration on MRI, CT and PET as well as specialist models do. title: AdaptReg: Skip-level FiLM Adapter for Task-Specific Adaptation of a Frozen Registration Foundation Model
desc: Longitudinal PSMA-PET/CT registration is a key step in assessing treatment response in prostate cancer, and it requires more than generic alignment accuracy: the deformation must preserve lesion volume, so that measured changes in metabolic tumor volume (MTV) and total lesion glycolysis (TLG) reflect treatment response rather than registration artifacts. desc: To develop and evaluate an uncertainty-aware multimodal learning framework for predicting radiation-induced xerostomia in patients receiving head-and-neck cancer radiotherapy. title: STORM: A Lightweight Structure-Free Model for Binding Affinity Prediction
desc: Accurately predicting a small molecule's binding affinity to a protein, a critical task in drug discovery, remains challenging. Recent machine learning--based cofolding models have reported accuracy approaching that of FEP---and at least one of them, Boltz-2, has already been widely adopted for affinity prediction---but they remain expensive for large computational screens and even more expensive for retraining on newly collected experimental data. desc: While deep learning offers tremendous promise for scientific and medical imaging, any failures and hallucinations (predictions that do not coincide with reality) are hard to pinpoint and can have serious downstream consequences. Uncertainty estimation techniques, such as conformal prediction, can help by predicting statistically valid error bars for a model's prediction. desc: Large language models are increasingly used for medical guidance, but women's health remains under-evaluated in benchmark design. desc: Routine electrocardiogram (ECG) reports offer scalable supervision for cardiovascular representation learning. desc: Wearable and smartphone sensors capture behavioral signals associated with mental health, yet inferring mental health outcomes from these signals has traditionally relied on supervised models requiring labeled data and offering limited insight into their predictions. desc: Autonomous software agents increasingly plan, implement, and test software with limited human oversight. desc: Prediction of pathological complete response before neoadjuvant chemotherapy may facilitate more tailored therapeutic planning for breast cancer patients. title: HardwareDx: A Foundational Graph Model System for Datacenter Machine Repairs
desc: The rapid scale-up of AI infrastructure has made datacenter reliability a cornerstone of the cloud business economy. Since hardware failures in hyper-scale AI clusters can stall multi-million dollar training workloads, the downtime of individual machines can cause outsized economic losses. To address this, we present Hardware Diagnoser (HardwareDx), an AI-driven hardware diagnosis system that applies a graph foundation model approach to automated datacenter maintenance. It allows a single model to diagnose many platforms and accelerate onboarding of new hardware products. desc: Powder X-ray diffraction (PXRD) is the primary structural evidence for covalent organic frameworks (COFs) and many other materials. desc: Biomedical tables often combine thousands of measured variables with only tens or hundreds of labelled samples, a regime that is poorly represented in general-purpose tabular benchmarks. desc: Objectives: Radiologists interpreting oncologic chest-abdomen-pelvis (CAP) CT must also detect non-oncologic conditions, yet existing CT foundation models are trained on single anatomical regions or on non-oncologic data. title: Spectral Vision Transformer for Efficient Tokenization with Limited Data
desc: Vision transformers tokenize an image into patches, which couples the token count to resolution and requires the embedding to be learned from data. desc: Large Vision Language Models (LVLMs) show promise in medical applications, but their inability to faithfully ground responses in visual evidence raises serious concerns about clinical trustworthiness. desc: Anomaly detection in medical images is a complex task, requiring the development of a robust model using only healthy patient data. desc: AI-generated bug reports have drawn criticism for unreliable claims and faulty reproducers that burden maintainers. desc: Clinical large language models are usually judged by whether the final answer is right. desc: What protects an LLM team when one teammate quietly goes wrong? Most multi-agent LLM work assumes cooperative partners and inspects chat between turns before acting. desc: Unlearning has emerged as an essential security and privacy-preserving solution in Machine Learning, enabling networks to support their clients' rights for data erasure, as mandated by data protection regulations. desc: Precise myocardial phenotyping at population scale is limited by the cost and accessibility of cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR), whereas electrocardiography (ECG) is widely available but reflects electrical rather than structural and functional information. desc: Failures in long-horizon embodied tasks can arise from how a vision-language-action model (VLA) is called or from its execution capabilities. desc: Biomedical entity linking maps textual mentions to concepts in structured knowledge bases such as UMLS or SNOMED CT. desc: Integrating IoT devices into household systems offers enhanced control over living environments. desc: Pretraining filtering is one of the most common safeguards for open-weight language models. desc: Hospitals record thousands of hours of surgical video annually, yet these archives remain difficult to search by content.
